newsitem.title: USA: ConEd sees little effect from Conn. power shortage.
newsitem.headline: ConEd sees little effect from Conn. power shortage.

text.p: A shortage of operating power plants in neighboring Connecticut is unlikely to have much effect on Consolidated Edison Co of New York, ConEd officials said Tuesday.
But they cautioned ConEd is limited in its ability to send any surplus power to Connecticut should hot weather and a surge in air conditioning push up the region's power demand.

"If we have a hot spell in our area...we'll try to help them," Jack Feinstein, ConEd's vice president of system and transmission operations, told a news conference on the outlook for the summer electricity market in New York City.
"We are limited to how we could support them," Feinstein said, adding any blackout or voltage reduction in Connecticut was not likely to affect ConEd's service territory.
ConEd serves about three million customers in New York City and Westchester County, just north of the city.

ConEd has only one major transmission connection with Connecticut, a 345 kilvolt cable that runs from its substation in Pleasant Valley, N.Y., to Northeast Utilities' (NU) substation in Long Mountain, Conn.

Power generation in Connecticut has been halved in recent months due to the ongoing outage of the 2,680 megawatt (MW) Millstone nuclear power complex and the planned permanent shutdown of the 582 MW Connecticut Yankee nuclear station.
Feinstein said ConEd could aid NU and other Connecticut utilities this summer by allowing them to import power via ConEd's transmission system from other utilities.
To meet an anticipated peak summer load of 5,085 MW, NU has the 2,500 MW capability to import electricity into Connecticut from New York, Canada and other neighboring areas.
All three units at NU's Millstone nuclear pwoer plant in Waterford, Conn., have been shut since March 1996 amid safety concerns raised by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
Last December, NU and its partners decided to mothball the Connecticut Yankee power plant in Haddam Neck, Conn.
At today's briefing, ConEd announced it expects to post a record in peak electric demand this summer at 11,705 megawatt (MW), up from the previous high of 10,805 MW set on Aug 2, 1995.
